html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. OAuth: open authorization; MCP: Model Context Protocol; PKCE: Proof Key for Code Exchange; CLI: command-line interface; SDK: software development kit; CRM: customer relationship management; REST: representational state transfer

  • Authentication versus authorization in a Claude system
  • How to spot security gaps in an integration
  • OAuth 2.1 for MCP: roles, PKCE, audience, scopes
  • Choosing MCP, API/CLI or agent-to-agent

2Authentication and Authorization

Running case

Lumen Advisory Reviews a Healthcare Client's Records Assistant

  • The assistant reads patient records through one shared service account with access to every record
  • A clinician asks about "my patients", yet the model could return any patient's chart
  • The API key sits in a mobile app

Authentication = who is calling. Authorization = what that identity may do. The model is never the access-control layer: it can be persuaded; code cannot.

Gap Why it is a problem Fix
Shared service credential for all users Every user acts with the broadest access; no per-user audit Propagate the end user's identity; use delegated tokens and the user's permissions
Authorization in the prompt ("only show the user's records") Can be bypassed by injection or error Enforce in the tool or data layer
Over-broad scopes or roles Larger blast radius Least-privilege scopes; split read and write
Long-lived tokens Theft window Short-lived tokens, refresh, rotation
Secrets in client code or prompts Leak risk Server-side secrets manager; environment variables; never in the browser or mobile app
No audit trail Cannot investigate Log identity, tool, arguments, result
Tools with destructive actions Injection impact Remove, or gate with human approval
Token passthrough Confused-deputy risk Server accepts only tokens issued for it
  • API keys: start with sk-ant-, are shown once, belong in a secrets manager, are read from an environment variable, should have expiry and be scoped to a workspace or service account; never ship them in browser or mobile code. Route calls through your back end.
  • Organizations on zero data retention cannot call the API from a browser at all (cross-origin calls are rejected).
Exam tip

"Which control closes the gap?" Usually enforce the user's permissions in code at the tool or data layer with the real identity, not a stronger prompt and not a bigger model.

3OAuth 2.1 and MCP

Point Detail
Scope Authorization is optional in MCP; for HTTP transports follow the spec (OAuth 2.1); STDIO servers should not use it and read credentials from the environment
Roles MCP server = resource server; MCP client = OAuth client; separate authorization server
Discovery Servers publish protected resource metadata; clients discover the authorization server
PKCE Clients protect the authorization-code flow with PKCE
Resource parameter Client sends the server's canonical URI so the token is bound to it
Audience validation The server must verify the token was issued for it
No passthrough Servers must not accept or forward tokens meant for other services; clients send only tokens from the server's own authorization server
Transport Authorization: Bearer header on every request; never in the URL
Scopes Request the minimum; the server's challenge names required scopes; 403 insufficient_scope triggers step-up with the union of scopes
Status codes 401 missing or invalid token; 403 insufficient scope; 400 malformed request
Client registration Client ID metadata documents preferred; pre-registration; dynamic registration is deprecated
  • Confused deputy: a server that forwards the user's token to a downstream API (or accepts any token) can be tricked into acting with authority it should not hold.
  • Custom connectors reach servers over the public internet and the user must trust the server; only connect servers you trust.
  • Skills and hooks can add deterministic checks around tool calls (Module 13).

4Choosing the Integration Mechanism

Mechanism What it is Use when Watch for
Direct API / CLI Your code (or a shell tool) calls a service Simple, one-off, fully owned, stable interface Duplicated glue per app; each tool schema maintained separately
MCP Open protocol connecting an agent to tools, data and prompts A capability shared by several applications, maintained independently; a catalog of tools Server trust, auth setup, tool bloat
A2A (agent-to-agent) Open protocol for agents to discover and delegate to other agents, across frameworks, staying opaque A separate agent owned by another team or vendor must be called as a peer Not a tool-call or SDK substitute; adds a network boundary
  • MCP and A2A are complementary: an agent uses MCP for its tools and A2A to collaborate with other agents.
  • CLI tools (for example git, kubectl) can be the simplest integration for coding agents, with permission rules around them.
  • Prefer MCP when the same capability serves multiple agents or applications, or when an existing server already exists; prefer direct API when it is a single app and the interface is small.
Exam tip

Authorization belongs in code with the real user identity; a shared service credential loses per-user permissions and audit.

Exam tip

MCP servers must check the token audience and must never pass tokens through; tokens never go in the URL.

5Exam Q&A

S1A records assistant uses one shared service account that can read every patient chart. Which change best fixes the gap?

  • APass the end user's identity to the tool and enforce that user's permissions in the data layer
  • BAdd a system-prompt line telling the model to show only the current clinician's patients in every answer
  • CLog every record access so that misuse can be found after the fact
  • DAdd a larger model that follows the instruction more reliably
Show the answer

Answer: A. Authorization must be enforced in code with the real identity; prompts and logs do not prevent access.

S2A mobile app calls the Claude API directly with a key embedded in the app. What is the right design?

  • ARoute calls through a back end that holds the key in a secrets manager and authenticates the user
  • BObfuscate the key inside the app binary so that it cannot be read by anyone who downloads the application
  • CRestrict the key to one model
  • DRotate the embedded key every week
Show the answer

Answer: A. A key shipped to clients is a leaked key; keep it server-side.

S3An MCP server receives a token issued for a different service and passes it to a downstream API. Which principle is violated?

  • AToken audience binding and the prohibition on token passthrough
  • BUse of the Bearer header
  • CDynamic client registration of every new client against the authorization server at each request
  • DPKCE for public clients
Show the answer

Answer: A. Servers must accept only tokens issued for them and must not forward others (confused deputy).

S4An MCP server returns 403 with error insufficient_scope and a scope for write access. What should a well-behaved client do?

  • ARequest every scope the server supports in advance
  • BRetry the same request in a tight loop with the same token until the server grants the extra permission
  • CPut the token in the URL query string to bypass the check
  • DRun a step-up authorization with the union of previous and required scopes, with a retry limit
Show the answer

Answer: D. Step-up requests the needed scopes, preserving earlier ones, and limits retries.

S5Which TWO are correct about MCP authorization? Select TWO.

  • AAuthorization is mandatory for every MCP implementation
  • BAccess tokens may be sent in the URL query string for convenience
  • CHTTP transports follow OAuth 2.1, while STDIO servers should read credentials from the environment
  • DServers must validate that access tokens were issued for them as the audience
  • EA client may reuse any token it holds across all servers
Show the answer

Answer: C, D. Audience validation is required; transport determines the mechanism; tokens never go in URLs.

S6Three internal applications need the same CRM lookup and update capability, maintained by the CRM team. Which integration is most appropriate?

  • AAn agent-to-agent protocol connection between each pair of applications
  • BAn MCP server owned by the CRM team and reused by all three applications
  • CA shared prompt that tells the model how to call the CRM's REST API in the same way for all three apps
  • DThree separate direct API integrations written by each application team
Show the answer

Answer: B. A reusable, independently maintained capability is the MCP use case.

S7A claims agent must hand a fraud-scoring task to an agent operated by a vendor using a different framework. Which mechanism fits best?

  • AAgent-to-agent communication, since a separate agent is being delegated to as a peer
  • BA direct SQL connection to the vendor's database
  • CAn MCP server that exposes the vendor's internal model weights so that the claims agent can call them
  • DCopying the vendor's prompts into the claims agent so that it can imitate the vendor's fraud model
Show the answer

Answer: A. A2A is for agents collaborating across owners and frameworks.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
AuthN vs AuthZ Who versus what; enforce AuthZ in code, never in the model
Gaps Shared credentials · prompt-based authorization · broad scopes · long-lived tokens · secrets client-side · no audit · destructive tools
API keys sk-ant-, shown once, secrets manager, server-side only, expiry
MCP auth Optional; HTTP = OAuth 2.1; STDIO = environment; PKCE; resource parameter; audience check; no passthrough; bearer header, not URL
Codes 401 token; 403 insufficient scope (step-up); 400 malformed
Choose Direct API/CLI simple and owned; MCP reusable tools and data; A2A delegate to separate agents
